# Troubleshooting {#sec-troubleshooting}

## Rendering

**`there is no package called 'reticulate'`, or the Python chunks fail**
: The chapters run R and Python side by side, which needs `reticulate` and a
  Python environment it can find. Run `source("scripts/setup_local.R")` and
  restart R; see @sec-setup.

**`cannot open file 'data/los_data.csv'`**
: Paths are relative to the project root. Open `HDS_M3.Rproj` so the working
  directory is right, or check `getwd()`.

**The published site shows old numbers**
: Nothing is executed when the site is published — GitHub serves the `_book/`
  folder as committed. Run `make site` locally and commit `_book/` with your
  chapter change. CI refuses to publish if a chapter is newer than `_book/`.

**A chunk containing `______` fails the render**
: It needs `#| eval: false`. Task code is shown, never run. `make check` catches
  this before you push.

## Working the exercises

**`Error: Syntax error: unexpected input`, or in Python `SyntaxError: invalid
syntax`, pointing at a line with `______`**
: Nothing is wrong: `______` is a blank for you to fill in, and no language can
  parse it. Replace every `______` in the cell — the prose just above it says
  what the cell should produce — and run it again. This is also why those cells
  are not executed when the booklet is built.

**I filled in the blanks and `check_metric_range()` says `[fix]`**
: The check is telling you the number is outside the range the exercise expects,
  which usually means the filter or the column is not the one asked for. Print
  the intermediate result — the filtered rows, or the column on its own — before
  the summary, and look at what you actually selected.

## Modelling

**R: `predict()` returns 800 rows when the new data has 400**
: `parsnip` wants `new_data =`. With `newdata =` the argument is swallowed and
  you silently predict on the training data. The most expensive typo in the
  module.

**Python: `ValueError: Expected 2D array, got 1D array instead`**
: `X = df["Age"]` gives a Series; scikit-learn wants a frame. Use `df[["Age"]]`,
  with two sets of brackets.

**The test MAE is suspiciously good (below 3 days)**
: You fitted on the full dataset rather than on `train`. Check the `data =`
  argument of `fit()`.

**The two languages give different numbers for the same model**
: Expected, if a random split is involved: `set.seed(42)` and `random_state=42`
  select different rows. See the callout in @sec-pipeline. Not expected for
  coefficients, which should agree to several decimals.

## On your own machine

**`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pandas'` in a `{python}` cell**
: reticulate has found a Python that is not the one this project declares.
  This is the most common local problem and has nothing to do with your code.
  Check three things, in order. (1) `getwd()` ends in `HDS_M3` — if you opened a
  parent folder, the project's `.Rprofile` was never read, and it is what
  declares the libraries. (2) `Sys.getenv("RETICULATE_PYTHON")` is empty — if
  you have set it, that Python is used as is and must have the libraries
  itself. (3) `packageVersion("reticulate")` is 1.41 or later; older versions
  cannot assemble an environment, so update and restart R. Then
  `source("scripts/setup_local.R")`.

**The Python console in Positron is labelled "Python (reticulate)"**
: That is the right one for `{python}` cells in a `.qmd` whose engine is knitr;
  R starts it and it is the bridge the chapters use. The separate "Python
  (System)" interpreter is not the one your cells run in, which is why
  installing packages into it does not help.

**`No such file or directory: 'data/los_data.csv'` locally**
: Paths are relative to the project root. Open the `.Rproj`, or check `getwd()`.

**A column arrived as text**
: `read_csv()` prints what it guessed; read that message. The usual culprit is a
  sentinel such as `"unknown"` in a numeric column. Fix it in the `col_types =`
  argument, not by editing the file.

## Rendering the booklet

**Rendering is slow**
: It executes every chapter the first time. After that `freeze: auto` replays
  the cached results, and only chapters you changed re-execute. Delete `_freeze/`
  to force a full rebuild.

**The printed worksheet is missing the tasks**
: `scripts/make_worksheet.py` builds it from the chapter sources. Re-run it after
  editing a chapter; the generated file in `print/` is not meant to be edited.
